+# CLAUDE.md — learning-environment config (NEVER commit; listed in .git/info/exclude)
+
+## How to help me
+
+I'm studying this codebase deeply before contributing. Target: a first bug-fix +
+regression-test PR found via differential testing. You are an instrument for
+interrogating this repo, not an author of fixes.
+
+- When I ask how something works: read the actual source first, answer with
+  file:line citations, then propose a small runnable experiment (DEV=CPU, tiny
+  tensors) that proves the claim. Never answer about tinygrad internals from
+  prior knowledge — this codebase moves fast.
+- Don't write fixes unless I explicitly ask for one.
+- If you find anything that contradicts this file, flag it to me instead of
+  silently working around it. Then we update this file together.
+
+## My setup
+
+- M1 MacBook Air: the only machine with Metal. CPU-vs-METAL diff tests run here only.
+- A Linux Codespace handles editing, the full test suite, and PRs.
+- `diff_test.py` (repo root, untracked) is my cross-backend differential harness.
+  It compares forward output AND gradients of each op across backends.
+  Env vars: `BACKENDS` (default `CPU,METAL`), `RTOL` (1e-3), `ATOL` (1e-5), `SEED` (0).
+- tinygrad is NOT pip-installed: scripts import it from the repo cwd. Run scripts
+  from repo root or set `PYTHONPATH=/Users/user/code/tinygrad`.
+
+## Verified gotchas
+
+Verified 2026-06-10 against local master `2c9d2c0d3` ("jit: memplan before compile").
+Note: local master was 2 commits behind upstream/master (`6e1b61f16`) at verification
+time; both missing commits are AMD/addrspace cleanups that don't touch any fact below.
+
+1. **There is no ShapeTracker.** `tinygrad/shape/` is deleted. Movement ops are
+   plain UOps: `GroupOp.Movement = {RESHAPE, EXPAND, PERMUTE, PAD, SHRINK, FLIP}`
+   (tinygrad/uop/__init__.py:131).
+2. **Shape semantics live in `UOp._shape`** (tinygrad/uop/ops.py:226). UOp-level
+   PAD/SHRINK args are `(offset, new_size)` per dim (ops.py:343-352). The Tensor
+   API still takes `(before, after)` / `(start, end)`; tinygrad/mixin/movement.py
+   translates (pad at :170, shrink at :192).
+3. **Indexing is generated at schedule time by "rangeify"**:
+   `get_kernel_graph` (tinygrad/schedule/rangeify.py:582) → `run_rangeify`
+   (tinygrad/schedule/indexing.py:153). `apply_movement_op` (indexing.py:134) is
+   THE definition of movement ops as index rewrites: SHRINK = `i+offset`,
+   FLIP = `(size-1)-i`, EXPAND = `const 0`, PAD = `valid.where(i-off, Invalid)`,
+   RESHAPE = div/mod + symbolic simplify (`_apply_reshape`, indexing.py:118 —
+   the comment at :129 calls the simplify "the replacement for the reshape view
+   merging code").
+4. **run_rangeify's 3-way rule** (indexing.py:186-225): realized → new ranges;
+   one consumer → inherit its ranges (this IS fusion); 2+ consumers → fuse only
+   if per-axis index exprs match across all consumers (valids get OR'd, :217),
+   else new ranges per mismatched axis + partial realize (:225). A partial
+   realize becomes an `Ops.STAGE` with `AddrSpace.LOCAL` (indexing.py:75-77).
+5. **`ending_ranges` is the broadcast guard** (indexing.py:165-237, 252-255):
+   an EXPAND that re-injects a reduced axis marks ranges as ending; any
+   elementwise/REDUCE producer with pending ending_ranges gets force-realized
+   (:228-237). This is why `x / x.sum()` is 2 kernels (verified: `r_16` + `E_4_4`).
+6. **`pm_remove_bufferize` is a post-pass cost model** (rangeify.py:331,
+   `remove_bufferize` at :239) that deletes removable STAGEs — recompute over
+   materialize — UNLESS the producer reads >3 buffers (:274) or contains a
+   buffer-reading reduce (:276-300). Both escapes are bypassed when `PCONTIG>2`.
+   This is why `e[1:] + e[:-1]` is 1 kernel with exp computed twice (verified:
+   single `E_15` kernel, two exp2 polynomial expansions in the C source).
+7. **Gradients**: `out.sum().gradient(*targets)` (tinygrad/mixin/__init__.py:447)
+   or `.backward()` (tinygrad/tens…[truncated for dataset]

+---
+description: Run a snippet under DEBUG_RANGEIFY and explain the trace + kernel line by line
+argument-hint: <python snippet defining tensors and an expression, ending in something realizable>
+---
+
+The argument is a short Python snippet defining tensors and an expression:
+
+```
+$ARGUMENTS
+```
+
+Do the following, exactly in this order:
+
+1. Write the snippet to `/tmp/trace_snippet.py`. Prepend `from tinygrad import Tensor`
+   if the snippet doesn't import it. If no `.realize()` / `.numpy()` / `.item()` call
+   appears, append `.realize()` on the final expression (bind it to a variable if needed).
+   tinygrad is not pip-installed: always run with
+   `PYTHONPATH=/Users/user/code/tinygrad`.
+
+2. Run:
+   `PYTHONPATH=/Users/user/code/tinygrad DEV=CPU DEBUG_RANGEIFY=1 NOOPT=1 DEBUG=2 python3 /tmp/trace_snippet.py`
+
+3. Rerun the kernel-producing step with source printing:
+   `PYTHONPATH=/Users/user/code/tinygrad DEV=CPU NOOPT=1 DEBUG=4 python3 /tmp/trace_snippet.py`
+
+4. Explain the DEBUG_RANGEIFY trace **line by line**. The format is printed by
+   `run_rangeify` in tinygrad/schedule/indexing.py (the `if debug:` block near the
+   bottom of the explicit-rangeify loop — read it first to confirm it hasn't changed).
+   Legend, column by column:
+   - `***` prefix = this UOp is in the realize_map (gets its own buffer/kernel boundary); three spaces = fused.
+   - first number = consumer count (`len(consumer_map[x])`).
+   - op name, then shape (`x._shape`).
+   - second number = `len(ending_ranges[x])` — pending ended ranges from consumers (the reduce-then-expand broadcast guard).
+   - `[...]` = per-axis ranges; `in -> out` arrows appear when input and output ranges differ
+     (movement ops, RESHAPE always); yellow axes are the realized (partial-realize) axes.
+   Walk the trace top to bottom (it's printed in reversed toposort: consumers first,
+   producers last) and for each realize decision, cite WHICH branch produced it:
+   - realize_map preseed (`pm_generate_realize_map`: COPY/CONTIGUOUS/STORE etc.)
+   - 3-way consumer rule (realized → new ranges / 1 consumer → inherit / 2+ → per-axis match-or-realize)
+   - ending_ranges broadcast guard (elementwise/REDUCE with pending ended ranges)
+
+5. Annotate the DEBUG=4 kernel source: map loads/stores to the original tensors, point
+   out recomputation (the same producer expression appearing more than once means
+   `remove_bufferize` in tinygrad/schedule/rangeify.py deleted a STAGE — recompute won
+   over materialize), and note which cost-model escape would have kept the buffer
+   (>3 accessed buffers, or a buffer-reading reduce).
+
+6. Finish with a one-paragraph summary: how many kernels, what fused with what, and why.
+
+Cite every claim about the mechanism as file:line into tinygrad/schedule/indexing.py or
+tinygrad/schedule/rangeify.py — read the current source, do not rely on remembered line numbers.

+---
+description: Show a symbol's definition, every call site explained, and the tests that pin it
+argument-hint: <symbol name, e.g. apply_movement_op>
+---
+
+The symbol to investigate: `$ARGUMENTS`
+
+1. Find the definition. Grep `tinygrad/` for `def $ARGUMENTS`, `class $ARGUMENTS`, or
+   `$ARGUMENTS =`. Show the full definition with file:line, and explain what it does
+   in a few sentences grounded in the code you just read (not prior knowledge).
+
+2. Find EVERY call site. Grep all of `tinygrad/` (and `extra/` if hits are sparse) for
+   the bare symbol name; filter out the definition itself. For each call site give one
+   line: `file:line — what the caller is doing with it`. Group call sites by file.
+   Read enough surrounding context at each site to make the one-liner accurate — don't
+   guess from the call expression alone.
+
+3. Find the tests that pin it. Grep `test/` for the symbol name (direct usage) AND
+   identify the behavioral tests that would break if its semantics changed — start
+   from the call sites' subsystems (e.g. anything in tinygrad/schedule/ is pinned by
+   test/backend/test_rangeify.py; op semantics by test/backend/test_ops.py). List each
+   test file with the most relevant test class/function names.
+
+4. End with a "shape of the contract" paragraph: what invariants the symbol's callers
+   rely on, i.e. what a subtle bug here would break first. If useful, propose (don't
+   run unless cheap, DEV=CPU) a one-liner experiment demonstrating the symbol's effect.
+
+All claims need file:line citations from the current checkout.

+---
+description: Fetch upstream, summarize new commits by directory, deep-read scheduler/uop/codegen changes, flag CLAUDE.md rot
+---
+
+Catch the local checkout's knowledge up with upstream tinygrad.
+
+1. `git fetch upstream`
+
+2. Summarize `git log master..upstream/master --oneline --stat` (use `--stat` to see
+   touched paths). Group the commits by top-level directory of the files they touch
+   (tinygrad/schedule/, tinygrad/uop/, tinygrad/codegen/, tinygrad/runtime/, test/,
+   docs/, other). One line per commit: hash, title, what it touches.
+
+3. For every commit touching `tinygrad/schedule/`, `tinygrad/uop/`, or
+   `tinygrad/codegen/`: deep-read the full diff (`git show <hash>`). Explain what
+   actually changed mechanically — which functions, which rewrite rules, which
+   semantics — not just the commit message. If a diff references symbols you don't
+   know, read their current definitions first.
+
+4. Cross-check every claim in CLAUDE.md ("Verified gotchas" and "Env knob cheatsheet")
+   against what you just read. For each claim that a new commit invalidates or bends,
+   flag it explicitly: quote the CLAUDE.md line, cite the commit, and propose the
+   exact replacement wording. Do NOT silently edit CLAUDE.md — show the proposed edit
+   and wait for approval.
+
+5. Finish with a verdict line: either "CLAUDE.md still accurate as of <upstream HEAD hash>"
+   or a numbered list of proposed edits. Do not merge/pull master — fetching and
+   reading is the whole job; I decide when to sync.

+---
+description: Plant ONE subtle single-line bug in a chosen subsystem for a debugging drill; reveal nothing but the branch name
+argument-hint: movement-index | valid-mask | fusion | debuf-cost
+---
+
+This is a debugging drill. The category argument: `$ARGUMENTS`
+
+Category → target subsystem (read the current source to pick an exact line; line
+numbers below are conceptual, not fixed):
+- `movement-index` — the per-op index rewrites in `apply_movement_op` /
+  `_apply_reshape` in tinygrad/schedule/indexing.py (e.g. an off-by-one in SHRINK's
+  offset, FLIP's `size-1`, RESHAPE's div/mod ordering).
+- `valid-mask` — the PAD valid construction in `apply_movement_op`'s PAD case or
+  `convert_pad_to_where_to_keep_behavior_local` in tinygrad/schedule/indexing.py
+  (e.g. `>=` vs `>` on a bound, OR vs AND of valids in the 2+ consumer merge).
+- `fusion` — the 3-way consumer rule / ending_ranges logic inside `run_rangeify` in
+  tinygrad/schedule/indexing.py (e.g. inverted `all_same` check, wrong axis appended
+  to `_realize_axis`). Bugs here may manifest as wrong answers OR as gratuitous
+  extra kernels — both count.
+- `debuf-cost` — the cost model in `remove_bufferize` / `remove_noop_bufferize` in
+  tinygrad/schedule/rangeify.py (e.g. flipped comparison on accessed_buffers,
+  dropped `buffer_in_reduce` escape, wrong substitution filter).
+
+Procedure — follow exactly:
+
+1. Verify the working tree is clean (`git status --porcelain` — untracked files are
+   fine, modified tracked files are NOT; abort and tell me if dirty).
+2. Generate a 4-char random suffix: `openssl rand -hex 2`.
+3. `git checkout -b drill/$ARGUMENTS-<suffix> master`
+4. Read the target file and choose ONE line where a single-token change produces a
+   *subtle* wrong-result or wrong-fusion bug — it must NOT crash, must NOT break
+   `python3 -c "from tinygrad import Tensor; print((Tensor.arange(6).reshape(2,3)+1).sum().item())"`
+   (run this with DEV=CPU to confirm the bug is not instantly fatal), and should
+   ideally only surface on some shapes/ops so the diff harness has work to do.
+5. Make exactly that one single-line edit. Nothing else. No comments, no formatting noise.
+6. `git add -u && git commit -m "drill"`
+7. `git checkout master`
+
+Output: ONLY the branch name. Do not describe the bug, the file, the symptom, the
+category's mapping, or anything you read or edited. Do not show diffs. Do not leak
+hints in your phrasing ("good luck hunting in the scheduler" leaks). One line:
+`drill/<category>-<suffix>`. I will hunt it with diff_test.py and the test suite,
+then reveal with `git diff master drill/...`.
